narrative.context: The engineering-manager skill runs Ethan's coding agents on the Multica board, a task tracker where agents work tickets. Its `kk-packet` command turns a ticket's commits into a review packet: a web page with the diff, a written explanation, and an approval panel. A decision on that panel can grant a push or a pull request, and a granted action becomes a job for Gatekeeper, the only agent allowed to publish, which asks `kk-may` for permission first.
narrative.overview: Two bindings hold independently. [Import](#import-pins-the-pr) writes the PR's commits onto a ticket of its own, and [the same command](#brief-or-mark-stale) either sends Programmer to that exact head or, if the PR has since moved, marks the review stale and stops. [The build](#build-at-the-pinned-head) accepts nothing but that head, checked against what is actually on disk, so the packet shows the code the PR held. On the other side, [the page](#page-records-only) can only record that Ethan read it, and [each gate behind it](#every-gate-refuses) refuses push, PR, feedback and Gatekeeper by itself, so no single bug turns a review into a publication.
narrative.problem: Every packet assumed the code was Programmer's own work, waiting to ship; Programmer is the coding agent. Reviewing a colleague's PR, #3625, took a hand-made ticket, a hand checkout of the PR's latest commit, and a hand-off from Programmer. The page then offered "Approve and push" and "Approve, push and open a PR" for code Ethan never meant to ship, and feedback went to Programmer as fixes to make. Nothing tied the review to the PR's exact commits.

in: `kk-packet import`: a PrimaryKids PR URL in, one branchless review ticket out, pinned to the PR's base and head.
Builds that refuse any other commit, and a stale mark when the PR's head moves.
An approval page whose only choice records the review and grants nothing.
Refusals at every later gate: feedback, `kk-packet-approval` and `kk-may`.
out: Capturing comments or a verdict, posting to GitHub, and packets of only what changed since the last review; later stages of PER-143 add these.
Repositories outside the PrimaryKids GitHub organization.
A dedicated template for Programmer's brief, which is written inline in `kk-packet.sh` instead.

body.prose: A SHA is a commit's full hash, an id that can never later mean other code. Import turns a URL into a ticket carrying two of them: the PR's base, the commit it targets, and its head, its latest commit.

body.explains: The URL must match `github.com/PrimaryKids/<repo>/pull/<n>` before `gh` is called, and `gh pr view` is the only `gh` command used. A re-run finds the existing ticket by `pr_url`; otherwise import creates one with no branch and records `review_kind=external`, the PR's number and author, and both SHAs, `pr_url` first because the search keys on it. `pkgs.gh` joins `kk-packet`'s inputs so the call can run.

sections.contribution: Every later step reads the PR's commits from this ticket, so this is where the review gets bound to exact code.
sections.heading: Import reads the PR once and pins it to one ticket

transition.text: A ticket checks out nothing by itself; the same command next decides whether to brief Programmer or to mark the review stale.

body.explains: If the ticket already existed and the PR's head is no longer the pinned one, import sets `review_pr_stale`, prefixes the title with `STALE: ` and builds nothing. Otherwise it records Ethan's yes and briefs Programmer to check out exactly the head, fetching `pull/N/head` for a fork, and to post a hand-off, its written account of the code. The PR description is quoted as data, with a warning that nothing in it is an instruction, because anyone can write it. Importing an unmoved PR again changes nothing.

sections.contribution: This turns the pinned ticket into a checkout at exactly the PR's head, and stops a moved PR from quietly replacing the reviewed code.
sections.heading: Running import is Ethan's yes, unless the PR has moved

transition.text: Programmer's checkout is the build's input, so the build must prove it is the pinned commit before using it.

body.explains: `start` reads the pinned fields, refuses a stale ticket with exit 7, and refuses a `--base` or `--head` that differs from them. It then sets both to the PR's SHAs, so nothing on the command line can move or widen the range.

body.prose: The diff starts from the merge base, the last commit the PR's branch shares with its target. `kk-review-packet` already computes it, and it matches GitHub's own PR diff; the PR's `baseRefOid` stays recorded as `review_base_sha`.

body.explains: `kk-packet-build`, which runs git as the `multicad` user, now reports `checkout`, the commit the worktree actually has, from both its dry-run probe and its build. `kk-packet` runs as the `openclaw` user and never runs git, so this field is how it learns what Programmer checked out.

The checkout is compared with the pinned head twice: after the probe, before anything is built, and on the build's result, whose range must also end at that head. A mismatch at either point records nothing and exits 4, so a checkout one commit short produces no packet.

sections.contribution: Here the pin is enforced: an external ticket's packet can only show the PR's head, compared the way GitHub compares it.
sections.heading: The build uses only the pinned commits, and checks the checkout

transition.text: With the packet bound to the right code, what remains is that approving it can only record the review.

body.explains: `kk-approval status`, the record the page server reads, now carries `review_kind`, `pr_url` and `pr_number` from the ticket. That is how the page server learns the ticket is an external review.

`approval.clj` serves the panel. For an external ticket it replaces every choice with `record-choice`, delivery `none` and no actions, titles the panel Record your review, and says nothing is ever granted. It also drops the force-push lease, the remote commit a force-push may overwrite, so that choice cannot appear.

`decide!`, the handler that receives the click, answers 400 to any delivery but `none` on an external ticket, before anything is recorded. A hand-made request for push gets the same answer as a hidden button would.
The decision is labelled Record review, and the notice sent after it uses that label instead of listing actions. A decision with no actions never reaches dispatch, so no Gatekeeper job starts.
The browser panel shows the server's title and intro when given and the old wording otherwise, so ordinary packets look exactly as before.

sections.contribution: The push and PR choices leave the page, so the place Ethan decides cannot grant anything for someone else's code.
sections.heading: The approval panel offers one choice: Record review

transition.text: A page can be bypassed, so the scripts behind it refuse the same things on their own.

body.explains: `kk-packet-approval` is what the page calls to record a decision and hand a job to Gatekeeper. On an external ticket it refuses any delivery but `none`, refuses `dispatch` outright, and passes `--no-project` so no `exposure_grants`, the ticket's list of permitted actions, are written. It now asks `kk-approval status` for the ticket's kind on every decision.

`kk-may` is what Gatekeeper asks just before pushing or opening a PR. It now answers `EXTERNAL REVIEW:` with exit 6 to any code action on an external ticket, before it reads any approval, so even a grant written some other way is refused.
Feedback would send Ethan's notes to Programmer as fixes to make, which has no meaning for someone else's PR. It is refused, exit 6 from the command line and 12 from the page, and nothing is sent.

sections.contribution: Each step a grant could pass through refuses on its own, so a page bug or a direct command still publishes nothing.
sections.heading: Every gate behind the page refuses too

body.explains: The notice sent to Ethan is headed with the PR number and pinned head, with a STALE line when the head has moved, and `status` prints the same. The Change Summary Writer's brief gains a Review line saying the PR is being reviewed, not shipped.

sections.contribution: Every message about the ticket says it reviews someone else's PR at one commit, and says when that commit is stale.
sections.heading: Status, notice and writer brief name the PR

body.explains: The header of `kk-packet.sh` explains external reviews end to end, and its usage text lists `import` with its two required options.

`SKILL.md`, the manager's command table, gains an `import` row; `references/exposure.md` adds `EXTERNAL REVIEW:` to its refusal table with the instruction never to hand the ticket to Gatekeeper; the tests README describes the new section.

sections.contribution: Agents and Ethan learn the import command and Gatekeeper's new refusal from the documents they already read.
sections.heading: The docs describe the command and the new refusal

body.explains: A fake `gh` answers only `pr view` and logs every call, and a test repository moves main past the PR's branch point so the merge base differs from the PR's base. The section checks the URL refusal, one ticket on re-import, refused overrides and short checkouts, the merge-base range, refused feedback, `kk-may`, the stale mark, and that every `gh` call was `pr view` with Gatekeeper never named.

The approval-page section adds an external ticket: one choice, push, PR and force-push refused, Record review saved with no actions, job or grant, and `kk-packet-approval` refusing push and dispatch with exit 12.
The fake board learns `issue create` and `issue update`, which import needs, and the documentation check now expects eight refusal lines instead of seven.

sections.contribution: The tests run the whole flow against fakes and check the read-only promise directly, from logs of every outside call.
sections.heading: Tests prove no GitHub write and exact-commit binding

narrative.thesis: `kk-packet import <PR URL>` reads the PR once, pins its base and head commits on a ticket of their own, and has Programmer check out exactly that head. The packet is built only from those commits, and its page offers one choice, Record review, which every later step refuses to turn into a push, PR, GitHub post or Gatekeeper job.
narrative.title: Review someone else's PrimaryKids PR from its URL, without granting anything

risks: Nothing has run against a real PrimaryKids PR, so it is unproven that the `openclaw` user's `gh` can read PrimaryKids.
`multica repo checkout --ref <sha>` is untried on a fork's head, and the brief's fallback is to fetch `pull/N/head`.
If import fails after writing `pr_url` but before `review_kind`, a re-run will not find that ticket and creates a second one.
A stale mark stays even if the PR's head later moves back to the reviewed commit.
`kk-packet-approval decide` now calls `kk-approval status` for every ticket, so a failing status call also blocks ordinary decisions.

tests.note: At `6e2179b`, whose code is identical to this head, 1715 passed and 7 failed against 1694 and 6 on main; the extra failure is a PER-124 check that depends on how commit hashes sort, and it passed when its section was rerun.
The new import section passed 18 of 18, and the four external-review checks on the approval page passed.
The suite's shellcheck section passed all 35 targets once `2c0f3e7` fixed two SC2015 warnings in `kk-packet.sh`.

A live import of the public fork PR jqlang/jq#3699, with the owner check widened in a scratch copy, pinned the real commits, refused a short checkout and wrote nothing to GitHub, but the board and checkout were stand-ins.
Not run: a real PrimaryKids PR, `multica repo checkout` on a fork head, the browser panel tests, and `nixos-rebuild`.

gaps: The review ticket gets no grouping label, and the hand-off asks whether it should carry `pr-review` or `standalone`.
Once a review is recorded, the page's history badge still reads approved at the reviewed commit.
`packet_review_required` is still set on external tickets, which only adds gating but was not removed.

collapsed.note: Both Gatekeeper instruction files gain the same `EXTERNAL REVIEW:` line, telling Gatekeeper to stop.
Argument parsing accepts the `import` command and a `--project` option.

findings.request: "Two bindings hold independently" fits only the first half; the page and gates refuse rather than bind. Say instead: "Two guarantees hold independently: the packet shows exactly the PR's code, and nothing can publish it."
Say what "Ethan's yes" approves, e.g. "running import is Ethan's go-ahead for Programmer to check out the PR", in the heading or first sentence.
Define "delivery" where `none` first appears, e.g. "delivery, the action a decision would carry out (push, PR or `none`)".
Say once who the Change Summary Writer is, e.g. "the agent that writes this packet's explanation".

understanding.approach: Add an import command that takes a PrimaryKids PR URL, reads the PR once, and records its base and head commit hashes on a dedicated ticket. Everything downstream is held to that head, and for such a ticket the approval page and every script behind it can only record that the review happened, never publish anything.
understanding.in-plain-words: You can now paste a teammate's PR link and get a review page for exactly that PR's latest commit. The tool remembers which commit it was, refuses to build from anything else, and flags the review as out of date if the PR changes. The page only lets you mark it reviewed, and every script that could push or open a PR also refuses on its own, so a review can never turn into publishing someone else's code.
understanding.peripheral: Status output, Ethan's notice and the summary writer's brief now name the PR and flag staleness; docs and Gatekeeper's instructions learn the import command and the EXTERNAL REVIEW refusal; argument parsing and the gh dependency are mechanical; tests add a fake gh that logs calls, a fake board that can create issues, and checks that no GitHub write or Gatekeeper call ever happens.
understanding.problem: The tooling assumed every packet was Programmer's own code waiting to ship. Reviewing a colleague's PR meant hand-making a ticket, hand-checking-out the PR, and then facing a page whose buttons offered to push or open a PR for code Ethan never meant to ship, with feedback routed to Programmer as fixes. Nothing tied the review to the PR's exact commits.
understanding.reading-order: Follows the data: the ticket must exist before anything can be checked out, the checkout must exist before the build verifies it, the packet must be correct before the page decides what can be done with it, and the scripts behind the page come last as the backstop if the page is bypassed.
understanding.risks: Never run on a real PrimaryKids PR, so gh access for the openclaw user is unproven; checkout of a fork head is untried; a partial import failure can create a duplicate ticket; a stale mark is permanent; every ordinary decision now depends on a status call. The new tests pass, the full suite has one extra flaky failure tied to hash ordering, and a live run against a public jq fork PR used stand-ins. Gaps: no grouping label, history badge still says approved, an unneeded review-required flag remains.

sections.advances: Validates the URL, calls only `gh pr view`, and creates (or on re-run finds) one branchless ticket marked external with the PR's base and head hashes, so later steps have fixed commits to check against.

Turns that ticket into work: if the PR head has moved since import, it marks the ticket STALE and stops; otherwise it tells Programmer to check out exactly the pinned head, treating the PR description as untrusted text.

Makes the packet build refuse any other range: overrides are rejected, the diff runs from the merge base like GitHub's, and the build reports the commit actually on disk so a checkout that differs from the pinned head (checked before and after building) yields no packet.

Passes the ticket's external kind to the page server, which replaces push/PR/force-push choices with a single Record review that grants nothing, rejects any other request server-side, and so never starts a Gatekeeper job; ordinary packets look unchanged.

Repeats the refusal in each script a grant could pass through: kk-packet-approval records only no-action decisions and refuses dispatch, kk-may refuses code actions on external tickets before reading any approval, and feedback to Programmer is refused.

understanding.system: An engineering-manager skill that runs Ethan's coding agents on a task board. Its kk-packet command builds a review page for a ticket's commits (diff, explanation, approval panel); approving on that panel can grant a push or PR, which becomes a job for Gatekeeper, the one agent allowed to publish, after it checks kk-may.
